blocks.title: Build and operate on Cloudflare with current, official guidance
blocks.description: Give Vetta Cloudflare's platform knowledge, project-aware Wrangler practices, live documentation and optional account access in one selectable package.

showcase.user_prompt: Review this Worker, add the right storage binding, test it locally and prepare a safe deployment plan.
showcase.assistant_reply: I’ll inspect the project, check current Cloudflare guidance, apply Workers best practices, and keep deployment or account changes behind your approval.

blocks.title: Choose only the Cloudflare capabilities you need

items.title: Design with platform context
items.description: Cover Workers, Pages, storage, AI, networking and security with retrieval-first official guidance.

items.title: Develop and review projects
items.description: Use project-local Wrangler conventions and review Workers code for production risks before deployment.

items.title: Look up or operate live services
items.description: Search public documentation without signing in, or separately authorize account operations when needed.

items.title: Select package members
items.description: Install the platform guide, Wrangler guidance, Workers review, public documentation or account connection in any combination.

items.title: Authorize only if needed
items.description: The documentation connection is public. The account connection opens Cloudflare's browser authorization and should receive the smallest useful scope.

items.title: Describe the outcome and boundary
items.description: Open your project and say what to build, review or inspect. State whether live changes are allowed before Vetta acts.

blocks.title: Live operations need deliberate approval
blocks.content: Wrangler and the authorized account connection can deploy or modify real Cloudflare resources, and some services may incur charges. Review the target account, environment, permissions and commands; prefer test resources and least privilege.

blocks.title: No hidden local MCP runtime
blocks.content: Both connections use Cloudflare-hosted services. Public documentation needs no login; account operations use browser authorization rather than a token pasted into chat. Wrangler remains a project-local dependency and is not globally installed by this package.
